corrections.critique: Strongest feature: Craig directly connects the successive-addition thesis to the central finite-past burden and clearly contrasts begun upward enumeration with a purportedly beginningless sequence terminating at the present. Principal limitation: the impossibility of reaching infinity through repeated addition from an initial stage does not establish that a beginningless history was formed or traversed from infinity, so the countdown description question-beggingly imports a commencement the history denies. Live burden: Craig must independently demonstrate why successive temporal occurrence ending presently constitutes construction of an actually infinite totality, while answering the no-first-stage alternative. Locked score: The mixed 68-point result properly rewards central relevance but discounts materially overstated necessity, unstable formation terminology, absent qualification, and insufficient warrant.
